title: More than a third of Russian companies forgo annual bonuses in 2026
content_preview: In total, 46.9% of Russian companies do not plan to pay employees end-of-year bonuses, with 36.2% forgoing bonuses only in 2026, despite having paid them a year earlier. The findings come from a survey of 1,076 companies across Russia conducted by Aktion Bukhgalteriya , Forbes Russia reported. Another 20.4% of respondents have postponed their bonus decisions indefinitely. Only 22.3% of those surveyed said they would pay bonuses to all employees. Another 10.4% said they would reward only part of their staff. A decline in this year’s financial results was the leading reason cited for skipping bonuses, named by 56.9% of survey respondents. Another 8.8% pointed to taxes and insurance contributions as the deciding factor. Experts attribute the trend to rising business costs. Russia’s corporate profit tax rose from 20% to 25% in 2025, and the value-added tax rose from 20% to 22% starting in 2026, alongside a lowered threshold for qualifying for the simplified tax system. At the same time, weak demand and a high key interest rate have made loans too expensive, while rising production costs are squeezing profitability and forcing companies to cut spending. Employees of small businesses will be hit hardest by these changes, according to Aktion Bukhgalteriya. Decisions at these companies more often hinge on a single person and current revenue. Large businesses, which have reserves and formalized bonus programs, will continue paying bonuses. However, some companies may replace annual bonuses with quarterly bonuses, paid training, or non-monetary incentives to avoid a buildup of financial obligations by December, experts say. title: ‘The smell of death is everywhere’: Inside the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where hundreds are trapped without food, electricity, or medicine
content_preview: A view of Oleshky Since 2022, residents of Oleshky in Ukraine’s Kherson region have lived under occupation. In 2023, the city was flooded after the Kakhovka dam was blown up: the flooding destroyed dozens of residential blocks and all of its infrastructure. In the fall of 2026, Oleshky found itself cut off. There’s a humanitarian catastrophe there: the city has no electricity, food, or medicine. Every way out is mined and blocked by Russian troops. Meduza spoke to people who have miraculously managed to stay in touch with those who remain in Oleshky. Here’s what they told us. ‘The harvest was so plentiful there was nowhere to put it’ “Oh, it smells amazing here!” Svitlana (not her real name), a former resident of Oleshky who fled the city in 2022 because of the war, smiles as she recalls her garden — and the compliments her friend Nina used to pay it. Before the full-scale war, Nina used to bring her homemade milk every Thursday. “I had [about a third of an acre] of land, and I planted peony bushes all along the perimeter. The scent was intoxicating!” Svitlana says. “Nina asked why I didn’t take the flowers to market. But how could I sell something so beautiful?” Svitlana’s yard brimmed with flowers until autumn, and hers wasn’t the only one. “It was as if the townspeople were competing over whose front garden was more lavish. Oleshky bloomed and smelled wonderful.” Svitlana calls the land she lived on for three decades “rodiucha,” which translates from Ukrainian as “fertile”: Stick a branch in the ground and it will sprout. title: A Ukrainian missile strike killed 20 Russian officers in occupied Donetsk. It was the largest known loss of Russian officers in a single attack since the invasion, Mediazona reports.
content_preview: A Ukrainian missile strike on Donetsk on August 26 killed 20 Russian military officers, Mediazona reported. The outlet said this was the largest number of Russian army officers killed in a single incident since the war began. The officers served at the headquarters of the Central Military District and the 41st Combined Arms Army. Mediazona confirmed their deaths by cross-checking personnel rosters against probate records and reviewing obituaries of high-ranking officers published over the past month. Denis Pushilin, the head of the annexed Donetsk People’s Republic, said on August 26 that Ukrainian forces had struck the area around the Donetsk City shopping mall with Storm Shadow missiles. He said eight civilians had been wounded but gave no information about military casualties. An Izvestia correspondent at the scene reported in a post that 10 people had been killed, but the post was later deleted . title: Montenegro detains Russian pro-war blogger behind Rybar, a Telegram channel with 1.5 million subscribers
content_preview: Montenegrin authorities detained Mikhail Zvinchuk, creator of the Z channel Rybar, local outlets Vijesti and Pobjeda reported. Zvinchuk, his wife, and several staff members were detained on the morning of October 9 in the city of Risan as part of an operation by Montenegro’s police and National Security Agency. Montenegrin media reported that the operation aimed to curb the “hybrid activity” of a network of channels that British and American authorities link to the spread of Kremlin propaganda. Mikhail Zvinchuk is a former press service employee of Russia’s Defense Ministry. He created the Telegram channel Rybar — which now has more than 1.5 million subscribers — with his colleague Denis Shchukin. The Bell reported that Yevgeny Prigozhin, founder of the Russian mercenary group Wagner, helped fund the channel. In late September, journalists at the Czech outlet Seznam Zprávy found that Rybar representatives work in Europe and regularly interview politicians, journalists, and experts. Czech law enforcement authorities detained and questioned Russian citizens Vitaly Chashchukhin and Igor Dolmatov, who are linked to Rybar, and ordered them to leave the country. title: Ukrainian grandmother released after Russia had her arrested in Kazakhstan on kidnapping charges. She’d traveled there to retrieve her grandson.
content_preview: Liubov Rozhanska, a Ukrainian citizen detained in Kazakhstan at Russia’s request, has been released, her lawyer, Alexei Pryanishnikov, told Vot Tak. “The detention period had expired. Since no pretrial restriction had been assigned, she was released from the detention facility,” he said. He said Rozhanska was released as early as October 4. She then spent several days on the grounds of the Ukrainian embassy before leaving Kazakhstan for Odesa. Rozhanska had flown to Kazakhstan from Istanbul in early October to pick up her grandson, who was to be brought from Russia. The boy’s mother had taken him from Ukraine to Russia in 2021. According to Pryanishnikov, the boy’s father had allowed only a temporary trip, but the boy and his mother never returned to Ukraine and instead obtained Russian citizenship. Ukrainian courts, including Ukraine’s Supreme Court, ruled that the boy should live with his father. Relatives of the boy’s mother contacted Rozhanska and offered to hand the boy over to her in Kazakhstan. At the same time, Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) directorate in the Kaliningrad region, where the mother and boy live, had petitioned a court for an arrest warrant against Rozhanska on charges of attempted kidnapping. When Rozhanska flew to Astana from Istanbul, she was detained at the airport at Russia’s request. Rozhanska’s lawyer insists that his client was carrying out the ruling of Ukrainian courts that determined the boy should live with his father. title: Ukrainian investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach detained in Vienna while searching for former prosecutor general who fled Ukraine
content_preview: Ukrainska Pravda reported on the evening of October 8 that Mykhailo Tkach, head of the outlet’s investigative journalism department, had been detained in Vienna while on assignment for the paper. The reason for his detention is unknown. The outlet said the assignment involved tracking down Ruslan Kravchenko, Ukraine’s former prosecutor general, who left the country after anti-corruption agencies searched his premises in early September. Ukraine’s embassy in Austria has asked Austrian authorities for information about Tkach’s detention, said Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi. A Ukrainian consul met with Tkach and was able to speak with him, but the journalist remains in custody. title: Russia’s air attacks are disrupting daily life across Ukraine. Here’s how five major cities are adapting to the growing danger.
content_preview: Jet-powered drones, which Russia began using extensively in late summer 2026, have changed the rhythm of life in Ukraine’s major cities. Air raid sirens now sound constantly, and strikes hit factories, warehouses, train stations, shopping malls, business centers, gas stations, and even kindergartens. Residents have been forced to adapt to the new challenges the war is bringing. With help from colleagues at other regional outlets, Ukrainska Pravda examined how constant attacks and alerts are changing everyday life in five major cities in eastern and central Ukraine: Kyiv, Odesa, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, and Kharkiv. Meduza summarizes its reporting. Kharkiv Entrance to an underground school in Kharkiv, May 31, 2024 Business : Kharkiv is near the front line, and air raid sirens sound about 10 times a day on average. Even so, its factories have stayed open, and entrepreneurs are registering new companies. Shopping malls keep operating during air raid alerts, although some stores close. At one mall, stores also rent space in the parking area, which is considered a shelter. Restaurants and other establishments close between 8 and 10 p.m., and stores between 9 and 10 p.m. Schools and hospitals : Children in Kharkiv attend classes either online or in underground schools. Hospitals have shelters with their own backup power. At the regional clinical hospital, an underground hospital is under construction and will be connected to the main building. Regular attacks and the arrival of wounded soldiers from the front are straining the healthcare system, so surgeons often postpone scheduled operations. content_preview: Update: Prosecutors have overturned the decision to open a criminal investigation into Nikita Tulupov, an investigator in the Lerchek case, TASS reported. Some of the jewelry seized during a search of blogger Valeria Chekalina’s home has gone missing, Interior Ministry spokeswoman Irina Volk said on Telegram. Authorities opened a criminal investigation into one of the investigators in the case against Chekalina, who is known as Lerchek. The jewelry “was not entered into evidence in the criminal case and was stored improperly, resulting in its loss,” Volk said. Volk said a criminal investigation had been opened into the investigator for allegedly exceeding his authority. She did not name him. title: Russia opens criminal fraud case against former co-owner of retail chains Lenta and Rive Gauche
content_preview: Dmitry Kostygin, the former co-owner of the Russian supermarket chain Lenta and the Rive Gauche chain, has been detained, the Russian business news outlet RBC and the St. Petersburg-based news outlet Fontanka reported, citing sources. On October 8, a Moscow court placed Kostygin under house arrest. According to Fontanka, Kostygin is accused of concealing Yulmart’s true financial position when he and accomplices signed a 2017 contract on Yulmart’s behalf with a company called Berks to supply equipment and machinery. Kostygin, a former co-owner of the retailer Yulmart, was named a suspect in a criminal fraud case in 2017. August Meyer, another co-owner of the chain, was also charged in the case. The businessmen were accused of misappropriating loans Yulmart had received from Sberbank and VTB for business development, with total damage estimated at 3.14 billion rubles. In 2024, a court sentenced Kostygin to four years in prison and Meyer to three years. Both were exempted from serving their sentences after the statute of limitations expired. title: Russia has spent a decade trying to stop people from bypassing internet censorship. Now it plans to spend nearly 60 billion rubles over three years on traffic filtering.
content_preview: Red Square, Moscow, March 16, 2026. Russia is preparing a new wave of restrictions on tools used to bypass internet blocks. The budget for the next three years includes a record 60 billion rubles for traffic filtering. The Digital Development Ministry wants to make mobile internet much more expensive for VPN users, and there are plans to put companies’ corporate networks under strict oversight by the Federal Security Service (FSB). Dozens of other restrictions have accumulated in recent years. We looked back at the main ones to show how the state has methodically cut Russians off from the free internet — and where we are on that timeline right now. VPN services were banned from bypassing Russian internet blocks (2017) On November 1, 2017, a new Article 15⁸ was added to the law “On Information, Information Technologies, and Information Protection” to address VPNs and other ways to bypass internet blocks: Measures to prevent the use within the Russian Federation of information and telecommunications networks and online resources that provide access to online resources and information and telecommunications networks to which access is restricted within the Russian Federation. The authorities did not ban VPNs outright. Instead, they required providers to filter their Russian users’ traffic and block access to resources on the banned list. If providers failed to comply, Russian telecommunications operators were required to block their VPN services on instructions from Roskomnadzor, Russia’s internet regulator. The only exemptions were for the authorities themselves and companies that needed unrestricted access “for technical purposes necessary to support their operations.” Internet providers were banned from explaining how to bypass blocks (2018) In February 2016, the Association for the Protection of Copyright on the Internet proposed administrative fines for promoting VPN use to access banned websites. Roskomnadzor supported the idea but proposed fining only internet p

title: IRGC says another supertanker struck a mine in Strait of Hormuz
content_preview: IRGC says another supertanker struck a mine in Strait of Hormuz Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy public relations said a second supertanker struck a sea mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said the vessel, carrying crude and preparing to exit the strait, hit a mine this evening, causing an engine-room explosion and fire. The statement accused the tanker of shutting all navigation systems and entering an unauthorized channel in violation of transit rules. Since yesterday, the IRGC said this is the third tanker alleged to have struck a mine and caught fire after transiting unauthorized waters.

title: 前三季度新开工重大水利工程数量超去年全年
content_preview: 从水利部了解到，今年以来，国家水网建设加速推进，前三季度新开工重大水利工程数量超过去年全年。此外，今年我国已完成2012处农村供水工程建设。预计到今年底，农村自来水普及率将达到97%。（央视新闻）
content: 从水利部了解到，今年以来，国家水网建设加速推进，前三季度新开工重大水利工程数量超过去年全年。此外，今年我国已完成2012处农村供水工程建设。预计到今年底，农村自来水普及率将达到97%。（央视新闻）

title: 日本报纸订阅率首次跌破50%
content_preview: 根据日本新闻通信调查会10日公布的2026财年调查结果，日本按月订阅报纸的受访者比例同比下降了0.3个百分点，跌至49.8%。这是自2008年开始这项调查以来的首次低于50%。（澎湃）

title: 卸任CEO后，苹果董事长库克再度到访中国
content_preview: 苹果公司董事长蒂姆·库克在卸任公司CEO后首次访华。10月10日，库克现身广州，探班iPhone 18 Pro咏春短片拍摄。在充满岭南风情的园林实景中，他探班了青年导演古天鸡与咏春拳传承人戴子龙的拍摄现场。 库克还表达了对中国传统文化的深厚兴趣与喜爱，并表示：“很高兴再次来到中国！在广州第一次通过iPhone 18 Pro镜头感受咏春的魅力，真是一次难忘的体验。”（澎湃）

content_preview: 美国司法部表示，正在调查五家停止对总统唐纳德·特朗普的行动进行联合报道的电视网络。此前白宫禁止多家新闻机构进入。司法部反垄断部门正在调查美国有线电视新闻网(CNN)、全国广播公司(NBC)、哥伦比亚广播公司(CBS)、福克斯新闻和美国广播公司(ABC)。这几家新闻机构组成一个电视转播联盟，共同报道总统活动并共享视频素材。“这个电视记者团的成员抵制报道白宫活动，”司法部发言人Emily Covington在声明中表示，“商业竞争对手之间的集体抵制行动可能违反《谢尔曼反垄断法》。”Covington说：“反垄断部门正在进行调查，以确定这些新闻机构是否违反了反垄断法。”（彭博）

title: 蚂蚁“灵光”开启小范围内测，新版对标“Meta Muse”
content_preview: 蚂蚁集团旗下AI产品“灵光”已于近日开启新版本的小范围内测，新版对标“Meta Muse”。 公开信息显示，今年9月，Meta推出个人智能体Muse。该智能体可介入用户日常生活，并持续跟进用户交待的事宜。 接近项目人士透露，灵光相关方向约半年前已开始筹备，期间迭代多个版本，计划本月全面开放。 该人士还透露，此次升级的核心，是灵光从能聊天、能生成应用的AI助手，转向拥有长期记忆、可主动推进任务的AI原生个人智能体。灵光新版本还能通过调用Skill和MCP，实现钉钉发信息、调用智能家居设备等功能。（新浪科技）

title: 中国科研团队发现并命名鲤科鱼类首个性别决定基因，命名“盘古”
content_preview: 记者从上海海洋大学获悉，经过十多年的探索研究，上海海洋大学胡炜教授团队与中国科学院水生生物研究所等单位开展合作，以鲤科代表物种黄河鲤为对象，发现了鲤科鱼类的首个性别决定主效基因，这是一个此前未见任何研究报道的新基因。为此，团队以中国古代神话中体现雄性力量的代表和开天辟地起始功能的“盘古（pangu）”命名该新基因，寓意其在决定鱼类雄性发生、开启雌雄发育命运的关键功能。（澎湃）

title: 李家超：皇岗口岸开通有三个重要意义
content_preview: 新皇岗口岸将于10月12日上午6时30分正式开通运行，为旅客和客运车辆提供24小时通关服务。港深两地今日（11日）上午在深方口岸区举行开通仪式。香港特区行政长官李家超致辞时表示，皇岗口岸开通有三个重要意义，包括体现落实国家规划、实践制度创新及促进跨境流动。 李家超指出，原有的皇岗口岸即将完成历史任务。重建后的新皇岗口岸明天正式开通，通关将更快捷、更方便。这个项目是港深两地同心协力、共建共享的标志性工程，是粤港澳大湾区互联互通的重要里程碑。随着香港与深圳的交通联系进一步加强，两地人流、物流、资金流和信息流将会更高效流动，进一步推动大湾区深度融合。 （大湾区之声）

title: How Low Can the Strategic Petroleum Reserve Actually Go?

content_preview: 美国总统特朗普新任命的白宫新闻秘书扎卡里亚（Katie Zacharia），曾在北京生活和工作，在中国知名律师事务所任职，并参与关注农民工子女的公益项目。她也掌握一定程度的中文。 据美国《新闻周刊》报道，现年42岁的扎卡里亚曾在美国加利福尼亚州佩珀代因大学法学院修读法律，毕业后前往北京，于2011年至2013年在中伦律师事务所国际业务团队担任律师。 在北京期间，她还参与公益组织“Compassion for Migrant Children”的工作，负责筹款及传播事务。该组织主要关注中国农民工子女的生活和教育问题。 香港《星岛日报》引述她过去的访谈称，目前扎卡里亚的中文能力虽然有所退步，但仍能听懂不少中文，偶尔会在听到中国人交谈时突然加入对话，令对方感到惊讶。 扎卡里亚的丈夫泰勒（Tyler Zacharia）同样有在华工作经历。美国《新闻周刊》报道，泰勒曾在北京工作，担任私募股权投资公司SGI Frontier Capital副总裁，负责中国、蒙古和巴西等新兴市场的投资业务，任职时间从2007年8月至2013年7月。 美国智库昆西研究所高级研究员西蒙（Denis Simon）告诉香港《南华早报》，扎卡里亚的北京经历可能为她提供有用的中国视角。她不仅通过美国国内政治辩论认识中国，也曾亲身接触中国的商业法律环境和公益组织工作。 特朗普星期五（9日）在社交平台Truth Social宣布任命扎卡里亚，接替今年8月离职的莱维特（Karoline Leavitt），出任白宫新闻秘书。特朗普称赞扎卡里亚长期坚定支持他，也是“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）运动的忠实支持者。 扎卡里亚今年曾短暂担任美国国土安全部发言人及公共事务副助理部长，随后出任特朗普媒体与科技集团旗下Truth Social的高级传播顾问。

title: 日本称四艘中国海警船驶入钓鱼岛周边海域 今年累计17天
content_preview: 日本方面称，四艘中国海警船星期六（10月10日）驶入存在主权争议的钓鱼岛（日本称尖阁诸岛）周边海域。 日本共同社报道，据日本第11管区海上保安总部（那霸）称，四艘中国海警船星期六下午4时05分前后相继驶入尖阁诸岛（中国称钓鱼岛）周边的日本领海，并于傍晚6时前后全部驶离，进入外侧的毗连区。 报道说，四艘船均搭载机关炮，日方巡逻船要求它们驶离领海。 据悉，这是中国公务船继9月10日后再次驶入尖阁周边领海，也是今年以来第17天有中国公务船驶入相关领海。 报道还说，包括毗连区在内，日本方面已连续63天在尖阁周边海域确认到中国公务船。

title: 中国男乒选手无缘中国大满贯男单决赛
content_preview: 在中国本土进行的WTT大满贯男单比赛中，中国选手未能进入决赛。 据澎湃新闻报道，星期天（10月11日）中午，世界乒乓球职业大联盟（WTT）中国大满贯男单半决赛展开较量。 中国选手周启豪对阵日本选手、新科世界第一松岛辉空，最终以2比4落败，每局比分为：6比11、9比11、12比10、11比7、7比11、5比11。 至此，中国男单止步半决赛，无缘争夺本届赛事的冠军。另一场半决赛中，中华台北选手林昀儒以4比3击败巴西选手雨果，晋级决赛。 中国乒乓球近期风波不断，在本届赛事上，三名球迷辱骂中国乒乓球教练员，被北京警方行政拘留。

title: 中国明起在东海等五处海域展开军事活动 包括实弹射击
content_preview: 中国多地海事部门接连发布航行警告，从星期一（10月12日）起，在渤海、黄海、东海和南中国海至少五处海域将陆续开展实装作业、实弹射击及军事训练，相关活动持续至17日。 中国各地海事部门从星期四（8日）起公布的航行警告显示，相关活动分别在河北、辽宁、江苏、浙江和广东附近海域进行，指定时段内禁止船舶驶入。 其中，秦皇岛海事局星期六（10日）公告，10月12日上午6时至16日午夜，渤海部分海域将开展实装作业。大连海事局同日宣布，12日上午11时至下午2时，黄海北部部分海域将进行实弹射击。 盐城海事局星期五（9日）也发布航行警告，10月16日上午7时至17日傍晚6时，黄海南部部分海域将进行实弹射击。 在东海方面，温州海事局星期四公告，10月13日至15日连续三天，将在浙江温州瓯飞滩以东海域开展军事训练，每天训练时间为一至两小时。 湛江海事局也发布航行警告，10月12日至16日，每天上午8时至傍晚6时，将在南中国海部分海域进行实弹射击。

title: 梅艳芳骨灰被盗案 港警重案组跟进
content_preview: 已故香港天后梅艳芳的骨灰被盗，香港警方称，已由重案组跟进。 据中新社报道，香港警方星期天（10月11日）回复中新社记者查询时表示，警方7月18日已接获相关报案。 香港警方称，经调查后，案件被列作求警协助，交由大屿山警区重案组跟进，暂未有人被捕。警方会继续与报案人及相关人士保持联络及作适当跟进。 综合港媒此前报道，梅艳芳2003年逝世，她的骨灰安放于大屿山宝莲禅寺海会塔。今年7月18日，有歌迷前往祭拜时，发现存放骨灰的龛位门牌螺丝出现松脱情况，进一步查看后，赫然发现里面的骨灰瓮已不见踪影。 目前家属已公开大屿山警区重案组联络电话及专用WhatsApp专线，供民众提供消息、照片或影片。面对骨灰至今仍未寻回的情况，家属希望各界协助寻找，让梅艳芳早日“回家”。

title: 中国天问三号拟2028年发射 2031年前后带回火星样本
content_preview: 中国计划于2028年前后发射“天问三号”探测器，并于2031年前后将火星样本带回地球。中国科研人员指出，人类要实现火星移民，仍须克服地球与火星之间的信息交流、物质运输及人员生存等三大挑战。 中国科学院上海天文台副研究员张佳骏星期六（10月10日）在《人民日报》刊登的署名文章《我们为什么要奔赴火星》中，重申中国火星取样返回任务的时间表。 张佳骏指出，人类目前已能向火星发射探测器，但尚未具备采集火星物质并将其送回地球的能力。“天问三号”计划于2028年前后发射，并在2031年前后携带火星样本返回地球。 他说，在地球与火星的信息交流方面，由上海天文台牵头建设的甚长基线干涉测量（VLBI）测定轨系统，能够精确测量飞往火星的航天器轨道，协助探测器顺利入轨。这项技术已在中国“天问一号”火星探测任务中获得初步验证。 至于人类在火星长期生存的挑战，张佳骏指出，火星表面低温、高辐射、低重力、低气压、缺水、缺氧，如何就地利用火星资源仍需探索。 他认为，水星接近太阳，金星环境恶劣，其他天体又太过遥远。相比之下，火星的条件好得多，有稀薄的大气、水冰，自转周期和季节更替与地球接近。因此，火星相当适合作为人类迈向星际文明的一站。 中国国家航天局今年4月已公布“天问三号”任务时间表。央视新闻9月初进一步报道，这项任务已进入初样研制阶段，相关技术攻关和科学准备工作正同步推进。 如果任务成功，中国有望率先实现人类首次火星取样返回。

title: 库克卸任苹果CEO后首次访华 现身广州探班咏春短片拍摄
content_preview: 美国科技巨头苹果公司前首席执行官库克卸任后首次访问中国，星期六（10月10日）现身广州，参观使用iPhone 18 Pro拍摄的咏春拳短片制作现场。 现任苹果公司董事长的库克在微博发文透露星期六到访广州，在一处充满岭南风情的园林内，探班青年导演古天鸡与咏春拳传承人戴子龙的拍摄现场。 库克现场观摩咏春拳表演，并与创作团队交流使用iPhone 18 Pro拍摄传统武术的过程。团队也向他展示了一份利用iPad Pro和Apple Pencil Pro绘制的“武功秘籍”。 库克在贴文中写道：“很高兴再次来到中国！在广州第一次透过iPhone 18 Pro镜头感受咏春的魅力，真是一次难忘的体验。”他也感谢古天鸡分享创作理念。 这是库克今年9月1日卸任苹果CEO后，首次以执行董事长身份访华。 苹果今年4月宣布管理层交接计划，由原硬件工程高级副总裁特努斯（John Ternus）接替库克出任CEO，并于9月1日正式完成交接。 库克转任苹果董事会执行董事长后，继续协助处理公司部分事务，包括与全球各地的政策制定者沟通。

title: 港深新皇岗口岸周一启用 过关最快五分钟
content_preview: （香港综合讯）连接香港与深圳的新皇岗出入境口岸星期一（10月12日）正式开通运行。作为深港之间唯一24小时通关的陆路口岸，新口岸将采用“合作查验、一次放行”模式，旅客过关时间可从原本约30分钟缩短至最快五分钟。 综合星岛头条网和网媒“香港01”报道， 新皇岗口岸 将在星期一清晨6时30分正式开通，改变过去深港两地分别查验的“两地两检”模式。 持有回乡证或港澳居民来往中国大陆通行证（非中国籍）的香港居民，北上离境时可选择使用香港身份证或回乡证过关。 车辆通关方面，新口岸将采用“联合一站式”车道。司机只须在车道的信息采集设备提交证件，完成体温检测和生物特征采集，即可一次完成香港海关、卫生署、入境处，以及深圳边检和深圳海关的五方查验。 在新模式下，车辆完成所有通关手续只需两分钟，比原本约10分钟大幅缩短。 据香港特区政府新闻公报，香港特首李家超星期天（11日）在皇岗口岸大陆口岸区，与广东省人大常委会主任黄楚平、中共深圳市委书记靳磊、深圳市长李运等官员，共同主持口岸开通仪式。 李家超致辞时说，皇岗口岸的重建，是粤港合作的重点项目，是香港对接国家发展战略，深度参与、贡献粤港澳大湾区建设的具体行动。项目也是港深两地同心协力、共建共享的标志性工程，是大湾区互联互通的重要里程碑。
